short_name: Turn-boundary server death
description: A long-running local server is reaped at the harness turn boundary; run_in_background binds, curls 200, then takes SIGTERM (exit 143). The editor's entire premise is a long-running local server.
notes: First-party verified across four documented attempts [V]. Only a Python double-fork daemon has ever worked here.

short_name: Gate 16-A probe
description: scripts/probes/probe-turn-boundary.ts plus the F1-F5 launcher ladder: launch, same-turn curl, END THE TURN, curl again in a separate tool call, confirm the pid is still in ps, repeat across two further boundaries and one eternity /clear.
notes: The single sequencing rule of the whole plan: run this first. F4 and F5 each require explicit user sign-off.

short_name: Server survival is unproven in pure TypeScript
description: O5 is unresolved: no pure-TS rung has been demonstrated to survive the boundary on this machine. F3 (a ~15-line POSIX sh launcher) is the preferred fallback because it keeps 100% of the server in TypeScript.
notes: [I] on which rung will pass. Honest residual: if F1-F3 fail and both F4 and F5 are refused, the browser-editor premise must be rescoped.

short_name: Gate 16-A blocks all server-dependent scope
description: Nothing server-dependent is treated as committed until Gate 16-A passes. S01 is the first slice of the plan and is the only slice carrying blocking=true.
notes: Mechanically enforced: S01 is a transitive prerequisite of S08 and therefore of every server-dependent slice.

short_name: tasks/S01-gate-16a-and-launcher-rung.md
description: The diagnostic slice that runs the probe, walks the ladder and records ADR-01 naming the passing rung and the exact launch invocation.
notes: Its QA section rejects any post-boundary check performed in the same turn as the launch.

short_name: Buildability of the product is decided in under an hour
description: The probe costs under an hour and decides whether the product is buildable as written, before any product code exists.
notes: [I] on the under-an-hour figure - inference, low confidence, not measured.

short_name: Cheapest disqualifying probe first
description: Sequence the whole plan so the cheapest experiment that can disqualify the architecture runs before anything expensive is built. Six diagnostic slices (S01-S06) precede all 68 build slices.
notes: CANONICAL CANDIDATE. Reusable beyond this feature: the E0 spike suite is the transferable shape.

short_name: Silent truncation of a pasted design system
description: A truncated CSS/HTML/SVG payload is syntactically valid and renders, so tokens cut at 40 of 62 properties are accepted with no error anywhere.
notes: Diagnosis would require diffing against a direction the user has never seen in full.

short_name: Envelope manifest with per-run terminator
description: Declared file list, per-file line counts, sha256 prefixes, smallest-first ordering and a per-run random terminator, validated at ingest with hard refusal and quarantine.
notes: Rejected payloads are quarantined, never partially applied.

short_name: The prompt is a lottery ticket not a build artifact
description: Step-3 output is non-deterministic and the model drifts, so the RESULT must be persisted as the artifact of record and the prompt kept for provenance only.
notes: Never plan to re-derive a system from a stored prompt.

short_name: Local Regeneration Mode as a first-class escape hatch
description: The identical prompt is run by a Claude Code path with zero pastes, making the claude.ai web hop a UX preference rather than a technical dependency.
notes: Directly attacks the most likely quiet death of the product: the paste marathon on site 2.

short_name: Localhost is not a trust boundary
description: CVE-2025-24010-class DNS-rebinding and cross-origin reach; Step 3 is an unauthenticated code-import channel whose payload is evaluated by the dev server and bundled into the published site.
notes: Eight security controls of record [V section 12.12], not the six carried into the inputs.

short_name: Eight-control security posture
description: Bind 127.0.0.1 only, Origin allowlist, bearer token, semantic-op wire format, path allowlist, idle shutdown, plus the two the source adds; the importer validates and quarantines.
notes: Must land with the first live editor (priority 12), not after it.

short_name: Two writers with no lock
description: The product encourages alternating between talking to Claude and dragging in the browser, so silent work loss is near-certain rather than a corner case.
notes: One writer: wb-server is the only process that writes layout.json, content.json and history.jsonl.

short_name: Optimistic concurrency plus a PreToolUse ownership guard
description: 409 on a stale ETag, editor.lock for processes, an SSE tab claim for the two-tab case, and a cheap fail-open PreToolUse guard blocking Claude's writes while the editor lock is held.
notes: Every save is a commit.

short_name: DOM as source of truth would be Dreamweaver 2003
description: If the DOM is the source of truth the product is a 2003 WYSIWYG, and worse, because Claude is also writing the source.
notes: Hard PRD constraint, not a note.

short_name: layout.json is the only source of truth
description: Pure render from layout.json + content.json + tokens; the editor never serialises the DOM; zero DOM injection for hit-testing; one renderer serves the design surface and LOCK.
notes: D3's re-render-not-copy-and-strip depends entirely on this.

short_name: Constraint editors are the experiment the market already ran
description: Wix Editor X sunset April 2024 and killed January 2025; Adobe Muse killed 2018/2020; Webflow's bidirectional cascade is a recurring forum complaint. The closest commercial analogue is dead.
notes: 'Move the hero headline 12px up' is one drag in a free canvas and a four-way CSS puzzle under D2.

short_name: DECISION-1 option B pulls the canvas into v1
description: v1 ships gridlines AND full constraint dragging. Section 18's editor-lite v1 scope is REJECTED; its timeline, its v1 scope-in list and section 13's gate budgets are stale and re-baselined. R47 retired.
notes: Decided 2026-07-26. Cost: +16-24 days, ~25-35 days against the revised baseline [I - inference, low confidence, not measured].

short_name: Epic E9 the canvas as seven sequenced sub-slices
description: S41 gridline overlay, S42 snap engine, S43 drag-to-place, S44 span and spacing handles, S45 keyboard parity, S46 override cascade with the pre-commit chip, S48 free-position escape hatch, S49 the tradeable tail.
notes: S49 is the only COULD in the entire 78-slice backlog.

short_name: D2 is exercised in the first shipping version
description: Demo 3 (S50) is the first real exercise of the constraint drag model, so R8 is either survived or diagnosed inside v1 rather than after it.
notes: The overridden recommendation's objection stands: this front-loads the highest-risk unproven mechanic.

short_name: Retire a risk by scheduling it early not by writing about it
description: R47 (v1 would ship without exercising D2 at all) is retired by moving the mechanic into v1, not by adding a mitigation paragraph.
notes: CANONICAL CANDIDATE. The cost is explicit and carried, not hidden.

short_name: Editor runtime leaks into published output
description: WYSIWYG editors leak their own runtime into the published site and there is normally no proof the shipped site is clean.
notes: And no way to unlock and keep editing without divergence.

short_name: Eight purity gates and a 32-check lock-time checklist
description: Re-render with editor:false, scrub, zero data-wb-* in dist/published (build-failing grep), two-build byte equality under diff -r, and 32 ordered checks = 28 base plus 4a, 11a, 13a, 23a.
notes: Eight purity gates [V section 12.5], not the five carried into the inputs; 32 checks [V section 13.4], not 28.

short_name: Byte reproducibility is unestablished by any consulted source
description: No consulted source establishes that the candidate bundler produces byte-identical builds across two installs. Section 12.8 only constrains our own generator's determinism.
notes: The documented fallback (normalised comparison) explicitly WEAKENS D3's proof and itself needs sign-off.

short_name: Run the reproducibility spike before promising the guarantee
description: S05 runs first; success criterion S4 is written against the spike's outcome rather than against a hoped-for guarantee.
notes: S05 is a transitive prerequisite of S67, so the gate cannot be built before its own feasibility is known.

short_name: A gate that fails spuriously gets disabled by whoever is shipping
description: Claiming a guarantee the toolchain cannot give produces a gate that fails for reasons nobody can fix, and it is then switched off - taking the real guarantee with it.
notes: Same failure shape as a false-positive wb verify: users learn to ignore it and the drift guarantee dies silently.

short_name: No AI aesthetic judging
description: NG1. The VLM judge loop and autonomous Wigum aesthetic iteration are not ported under any circumstances; the human is the sole aesthetic judge and machines enforce only machine-checkable correctness.
notes: VLM recall of aesthetic animation measured 0.16 [U - prior report, flagged unvalidated end-to-end].

short_name: Machine-checkable correctness is non-negotiable and human taste is not machine-judged
description: Split the acceptance surface: contrast, reflow, token purity, licence completeness and export purity are gates the human may not wave through; everything aesthetic is the human's call and is merely recorded.
notes: CANONICAL CANDIDATE. This is the line that keeps the rejected autonomous architecture out.

short_name: Acceptance-criterion ids collide above A90
description: A91-A97 are defined three times in the source PRD (section 7, section 12.17, section 18) and A98-A101 twice. The prior register recorded a two-section collision.
notes: Section 12.5 announces A91-A99 while its own section 12.17 table runs to A101.

short_name: Section-qualified citation as the interim rule
description: Every A91+ and every O31-O35 citation is written section-qualified until a renumbering pass lands. A1-A90 remain the criteria of record at 90, not 96.
notes: Interim only. The renumbering pass must reconcile three A91+ sets and four O31 meanings.

short_name: stories.json plus 78 task files
description: 78 slices across 20 epics and 26 stories; 188 FR ids partitioned one-to-one; 90 canonical acceptance criteria plus 180 slice-local criteria; 120 dependency edges forming a valid DAG.
notes: 394,515 bytes across tasks/; every file carries PM, Dev, QA, Dev Learnings and QA Learnings.

short_name: Exact requirement partition achieved
description: 188 FR ids defined, 188 claimed, zero unclaimed, zero undefined, zero double-claimed. Every requirement is owned by exactly one slice.
notes: Computed mechanically from spec.md and stories.json, not asserted.

short_name: One requirement one owner enforced mechanically
description: Partition the requirement register across slices with a script rather than by review, so both orphan directions are provably empty before any code is written.
notes: CANONICAL CANDIDATE. Cheap, mechanical, and it caught the citation-style gap in plan.md and tech_prd.md.

short_name: Four unsigned section-18 sign-off rows
description: Rows 4(c) rich-text-is-v2, 4(d) one-direction-only, 4(f) editor-still-lacks-zoom-pan-rulers-multi-select and 6 charts-partial remain unsigned. Section 18's own precondition bars any v1 build until every row is resolved.
notes: The backlog is complete and unstartable at the same time. DECISION 1 resolved rows 4(a), 4(b) and consequentially 7.

short_name: O4 topology ADR gates nothing mechanically
description: S04 (the topology spike and its ADR) has zero dependents; the editor shell S29 depends on S25 and S08 only. The invariant rule I1-I6 is stated in prose and absent from depends_on.
notes: Found mechanically during this analysis. Recommend adding S04 to S29's depends_on.

short_name: plan.md demo slice ids disagree with stories.json four-for-four
description: plan.md section 3.2 places Demo 1 at S30, Demo 2 at S41, Demo 3 at S51 and Demo 4 at S73; stories.json uses S28, S40, S50 and S72, and the task files follow stories.json.
notes: The carried defect list named only Demo 2 and Demo 3. plan.md owns the edit; nothing was silently fixed.

short_name: analysis-report.md and the CAGE trace
description: Cross-artifact analysis with mechanically computed coverage tables, a defect register carrying every known defect with its status, and this session trace.
notes: Emitted by /preeng.analyze after both upstream QA gates were confirmed APPROVED.

short_name: Pre-engineering completes with every contradiction visible
description: Eleven source contradictions, one dependency gap and one id-format drift are recorded with status rather than resolved, so the first build decision is made with the full defect surface in view.
notes: No defect was silently fixed. Every schedule figure carried is tagged [I], low confidence.

short_name: Record the contradiction do not resolve it silently
description: When two sections of a signed-off source disagree, carry both readings with their section references and name who owns the edit, instead of picking one and erasing the disagreement.
notes: CANONICAL CANDIDATE. It is what makes the 15 non-blocking issues in each QA report auditable rather than decorative.
